subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA routing, subprocessors, and edge/onramp onboarding
messages:
From: Juliana Alvarez <juliana@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: CCPA/CPRA: routing & subprocessors for edge/onramp use

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. A couple of follow-ups from our legal/compliance team as we move toward a pilot:

1) Role classification: our privacy team needs written confirmation whether Redwood will sign the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CPRA) addendum as a "service provider" (i.e., limited use/processing) or a vendor/contractor. That affects our required controls and downstream notices.

2) Subprocessor evidence: please provide an updated subprocessor list and any SOC2/ISO evidence for the infra providers that handle telemetry and prefix caching. We have an internal questionnaire attached — can you complete the relevant sections?

3) Routing/edge behavior: we have a hard requirement that certain patient-identified tokens (PHI-like identifiers in our test data) never route outside the US. Can you explain how Redwood's edge/onramp and fallback routing behaves, and whether geo-fencing can be applied at the request level? Any documented guarantees are helpful.

Can you loop in privacy and security folks and send a proposed timeline for answers? We need this in advance of our security review next week.

Thanks,
Juliana
Legal Ops | AcmeHealth

Attachment: Acme_subprocessor_questionnaire_20251112.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Juliana Alvarez <juliana@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA: routing & subprocessors for edge/onramp use

Juliana — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Aditya (security) and Naomi (privacy) to capture the technical controls and the DPA language. High-level answers below; we'll follow with attachments and a short mutual action plan by Thursday.

Quick answers:
- Role: Redwood signs standard DPAs as a service provider/Limited Use Processor for customers that configure the "service provider" addendum (we include the US-state addendum language for CCPA/CPRA scenarios). We are willing to confirm this in writing and to sign AcmeHealth's template with the limited-use carve-ins, subject to a few standard redlines.
- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor register and SOC2 summary. We will complete the questionnaire and highlight where telemetry is stored and which providers are used for KV caching and routing.
- Routing/edge: we support request-level region pinning so you can restrict traffic to US-only regions. That covers edge onramps and fallback routing — if US capacity isn't available we will fall back to an alternate US region; we do not route US-flagged requests to EU/APAC by default. We'll provide the precise configuration names and the relevant routing policy config snippet.

Next steps:
1) Aditya and Naomi to attach SOC2/controls summary and a brief technical note on geo-fencing and telemetry retention.
2) Redwood to return the completed questionnaire and DPA redline by Thu 11/13 EOD PT.
3) Joint call if Acme wants to walk through the routing config before your security review.

If that timeline works for you, we'll get the docs over today.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_v3.docx (docx, 55KB); Subprocessor_list_20251112.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Juliana Alvarez <juliana@acmehealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Nov 2025 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA: routing & subprocessors for edge/onramp use

Hi Juliana — Naomi here from privacy. A few concrete data points to help your review:

- Service provider confirmation: Redwood treats customer prompt data as customer content only. Under the service-provider addendum we do not sell or monetize customer content; our permitted uses are limited to performing the service, debugging when requested, and compliance obligations.

- Telemetry & limited use: We maintain telemetry for service health and billing; we can limit telemetry retention window down to 30 days for pilot customers on request. Sensitive data fields that you flag (we can document a list of JSON paths) are excluded from telemetry by default if you enable the "sensitive_field_masking" option.

- Subprocessors and evidence: Attached is our up-to-date subprocessor register and SOC2 report. Key subprocessors handling caching/routing: CloudCache LLC (KV cache in us-west/us-east), TransitNet (edge routing, US regions), and StorageCorp (long-term logs). We can provide redacted SOC2 attestations and AICPA contact for verification.

- Routing guarantee: we can add contractual language committing to US-only processing for requests explicitly marked with the AcmeHealth "us_only" header. That will be enforced by our routing layer and logged in request trace. Falls back: if US capacity is down, we will queue requests and return a 503 rather than route outside the US unless Acme opts into emergency cross-region failover.

I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a short config snippet you can hand to your infra team. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the header and routing policy.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Privacy Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_Report_2025.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB); routing-config-snippet.txt (txt, 2KB)

From: Juliana Alvarez <juliana@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@acmehealth.com>, AcmeHealth Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA: routing & subprocessors for edge/onramp use

Vanessa / Naomi — thank you, that is very helpful and addresses most of our asks. A few follow-up items before we close the security review:

- Please add the proposed contractual clause that: "Redwood will not route requests marked with the AcmeHealth "us_only" header outside of the United States. In the event of sustained US-region capacity outage, Redwood will notify AcmeHealth and queue requests for up to 12 hours; Redwood will only allow emergency cross-region failover with prior written approval from AcmeHealth."

- We received the completed questionnaire and the SOC2 summary — our security team will reach out if they need the unredacted report and auditor contact.

- Can we get a final DPA redline before EOD Monday 11/17? We want to include the US-state addendum language for CCPA/CPRA with the limited-use definition and the subprocessor notice timeline (14 days).

If you can confirm the clause language and timeline, we'll mark the security review as green and proceed to procurement.

Best,
Juliana
Legal Ops | AcmeHealth

Attachment: Completed_questionnaire_received.pdf (stated)
